evidence: This describes the experimental design.

claim: The APC/C isolated from S-phase cells served as a control.
source: The APC/C isolated from S-phase cells served as a control (workflow in Figure 1A).
evidence: This describes the experimental design, as shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The software is open source and available in two versions: an easy-to-use graphical user interface (GUI) version and a command line interface (CLI) version.
source: The software is open source and available in two versions: an easy-to-use graphical user interface (GUI) version as well as a command line interface (CLI) version to allow for integration into bioinformatics analysis pipelines.
evidence: This describes the software availability and formats.

claim: The APC/C was purified from each time point separately by co-immunoprecipitation using an anti-CDC27 antibody.
source: Prior to analysis of the peptide-resolved modification dynamics of the APC/C, the complex was purified from each time point separately by co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP) using an anti-CDC27 antibody (workflow in Figure 1A).
evidence: This describes the experimental protocol, as shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The protein digests of the co-immunoprecipitates from the different cell cycle stages were analyzed in triplicate using an LC-SWATH method.
source: The protein digests of the co-immunoprecipitates from the different cell cycle stages were analyzed in triplicate using an LC-SWATH method.
evidence: This describes the mass spectrometry analysis approach.

claim: The SWATH dataset was analyzed using a project-specific spectral library comprising 13,724 peptides representing 2041 proteins.
source: The SWATH dataset was analyzed using a project-specific spectral library comprising 13,724 peptides representing 2041 proteins (details in Material and Methods).
evidence: This describes the data analysis approach and the size of the spectral library.

claim: Two out of 12 technical replicates were excluded from the analysis due to low number of identified/quantified proteins.
source: Two out of 12 technical replicates were excluded from the analysis due to low number of identified/quantified proteins (one each from the 4 hr and 10 hr time points).
evidence: This describes quality control measures applied to the data.

claim: The analysis focused on bona fide members of the APC/C protein complex: APC1, APC4, APC5, APC7, APC10, APC15, APC 16, CDC16, CDC20, CDC23, CDC26, and CDC27.
source: As the APC/C is a well-characterized protein complex, we focused on the bona fide members of this protein complex, namely APC1, APC4, APC5, APC7, APC10, APC15, APC 16, CDC16, CDC20, CDC23, CDC26, and CDC27 (raw intensities of all peptides can be found in Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This describes the scope of the analysis.

claim: 248 out of 289 APC/C component-derived peptides (86%) met the criteria for FLEXIQuant-LF analysis.
source: In total, 248 out of 289 APC/C component-derived peptides (86%) met those criteria.
evidence: This describes the data quality and filtering results.

claim: Across the 248 quantified peptides, the median Pearson correlation coefficient between replicates was 0.98 (range: 0.96 to 0.99).
source: Across these 248 quantified peptides, the median Pearson correlation coefficient between replicates was 0.98 (range: 0.96 to 0.99) highlighting excellent quantification.
evidence: This describes the reproducibility of the quantification.

claim: Cell cycle-dependent modification dynamics have been extensively studied for CDC27 and APC5.
source: For the benchmarking of FLEXIQuant-LF, we focused on CDC27 and APC5. Cell cycle-dependent modification dynamics have been extensively studied for both proteins (Singh et al., 2009; Steen et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Singh et al., 2009 and Steen et al., 2008.

claim: 33 peptides corresponding to CDC27 were quantified with 55% sequence coverage.
source: We quantified 33 peptides corresponding to CDC27 (sequence coverage: 55%), of which nine peptides were classified as likely differentially modified within the time series (Figure 2A, magenta bars) by our FLEXIQuant-LF method.
evidence: This describes the quantification results for CDC27, as shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Nine CDC27 peptides were classified as likely differentially modified by FLEXIQuant-LF.
source: We quantified 33 peptides corresponding to CDC27 (sequence coverage: 55%), of which nine peptides were classified as likely differentially modified within the time series (Figure 2A, magenta bars) by our FLEXIQuant-LF method.
evidence: This describes the FLEXIQuant-LF classification results for CDC27, as shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Four CDC27 peptides were classified as possibly differentially modified by FLEXIQuant-LF.
source: Four peptides were classified as possibly differentially modified (Figure 2A, blue bars).
evidence: This describes the FLEXIQuant-LF classification results for CDC27, as shown in Figure 2A.

claim: One CDC27 peptide (31LYAEVHSEEALFLLATCamYYR50) was classified as outlier based on its raw scores and removed before RM score calculation.
source: One peptide (31LYAEVHSEEALFLLATCamYYR50) was classified as outlier based on its raw scores and removed before RM score calculation.
evidence: This describes the outlier removal in the analysis.

claim: Six CDC27-derived phosphorylated peptides were identified in the DDA data.
source: In total, we identified six CDC27-derived phosphorylated peptides in the DDA data (Figure 2A, orange stars).
evidence: This describes the PTM identification results, as shown in Figure 2A.

claim: FLEXIQuant-LF classified the unmodified versions of six CDC27 phosphopeptides as five likely differentially modified peptides and one possibly differentially modified peptide.
source: The FLEXIQuant-LF analysis classified the unmodified versions of these six phosphopeptides as follows: five likely differentially modified peptides and one possibly differentially modified peptide.
evidence: This describes the concordance between FLEXIQuant-LF classification and DDA identification.

claim: For the other four CDC27 peptides identified as likely differentially modified and for two out of three remaining peptides classified as possibly differentially modified by FLEXIQuant-LF, phosphorylations and/or ubiquitinations were described in the literature or deposited online.
source: For the other four peptides identified as likely differentially modified as well as for two out of the three remaining peptides classified as possibly differentially modified by FLEXIQuant-LF, phosphorylations, and/or ubiquitinations were described (Steen et al., 2008) or deposited online at http://www.phosphosite.org (Hornbeck et al., 2015) (yellow stars).
evidence: This describes validation of FLEXIQuant-LF results using literature and database evidence, with citations to Steen et al., 2008 and Hornbeck et al., 2015.

claim: Evidence of modification was found for all CDC27 peptides identified as likely modified and for three out of four possibly differentially modified peptides.
source: In summary, FLEXIQuant-LF demonstrated an excellent performance in detecting potentially modified peptides. We found evidence of modification for all peptides identified as likely modified in our study and for three out of four possibly differentially modified peptides.
evidence: This summarizes the validation results for CDC27.

claim: Relative to time point 0 hr (S-phase), the N-terminal region of CDC27 (amino acids 170–441) was increasingly modified after 4 hr (27% to 54%, average: 36%) and reached its maximum modification extent after 10 hr (between 55% and 81%, average: 65%).
source: Relative to time point 0 hr (S-phase) in our time series, the N-terminal region of CDC27 (amino acids 170–441) was increasingly modified after 4 hr (27% to 54%, average: 36%) and reached its maximum modification extent after 10 hr (between 55% and 81%, average: 65%) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This describes the quantification of modification extent for CDC27, as shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The CDC27 peptide spanning amino acids 442 to 456 (442ISTITPQIQAFNLQK456) showed an increasing degree of modification up to 48% modified after 10 hr.
source: The peptide spanning amino acids 442 to 456 (442ISTITPQIQAFNLQK456) also showed an increasing degree of modification but to a lower extent (up to 48% modified after 10 hr).
evidence: This describes the quantification of modification extent for a specific CDC27 peptide.

claim: 37 peptides corresponding to APC5 were quantified with 59% sequence coverage.
source: For APC5, two peptides (497FPPNSQHAQLWMLCamDQK513 and 35IAVLVLLNEMSR46) out of 37 quantified peptides (sequence coverage: 59%) were classified as outliers based on their raw scores and were excluded from further analysis.
evidence: This describes the quantification results for APC5.

claim: Two APC5 peptides were classified as outliers and excluded from further analysis.
source: For APC5, two peptides (497FPPNSQHAQLWMLCamDQK513 and 35IAVLVLLNEMSR46) out of 37 quantified peptides (sequence coverage: 59%) were classified as outliers based on their raw scores and were excluded from further analysis.
evidence: This describes the outlier removal in the APC5 analysis.

claim: Out of 35 remaining APC5 peptides, four were classified as likely differentially modified and five peptides as possibly differentially modified.
source: Out of the 35 remaining peptides, four were classified as likely differentially modified across the time points (Figure 2B, magenta bars), while five peptides were considered as possibly differentially modified (Figure 2B, blue bars).
evidence: This describes the FLEXIQuant-LF classification results for APC5, as shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Phosphorylated cognates for two of the four likely modified APC5 peptides were identified in the DDA data.
source: We identified in our DDA data the phosphorylated cognates for two of the four likely modified peptides (Figure 2B, orange stars).
evidence: This describes the PTM identification results for APC5, as shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Evidence of modifications was found in the literature for the other two APC5 peptides identified as likely differentially modified and for four of the five peptides classified as possibly differentially modified.
source: We found evidence of modifications within the literature for the other two peptides identified as likely differentially modified in our FLEXIQuant-LF analysis as well as for four of the five peptides classified as possibly differentially modified (yellow stars) (Hornbeck et al., 2004).
evidence: This describes validation of FLEXIQuant-LF results using literature evidence, with citation to Hornbeck et al., 2004.

claim: No evidence for modification was found for one possibly differentially modified APC5 peptide (99LMAEGELK106).
source: Interestingly, we did not find evidence for modification for one possibly differentially modified peptide (99LMAEGELK106). This could be interpreted either as a false positive classification or that this peptide has a hitherto undescribed modification on the methionine, glutamic acid or lysine residues.
evidence: This describes a case where FLEXIQuant-LF identified a potentially modified peptide without literature support.

claim: The FLEXIQuant-LF findings are in excellent agreement with the original label-based FLEXIQuant analysis of CDC27 and APC5, which identified the same protein regions as being modified to a comparable extent.
source: Overall, these findings are in excellent agreement with the original label-based FLEXIQuant analysis of CDC27 and APC5 (Singh et al., 2009), which identified the same protein regions as being modified to a comparable extent.
evidence: This describes the concordance between FLEXIQuant-LF and the original FLEXIQuant method, with citation to Singh et al., 2009.

claim: The extent of modification was lower in FLEXIQuant-LF analysis compared to the original FLEXIQuant study.
source: It was noted that compared to the original FLEXIQuant study the extent of modification was lower in our novel FLEXIQuant-LF analysis.
evidence: This describes a difference between FLEXIQuant-LF and the original FLEXIQuant method.

claim: A highly probable explanation for the lower modification extent in FLEXIQuant-LF is that there was a basal modification level of up to 20% for some peptides in S-phase.
source: A highly probable explanation for this phenomenon could be that there was a basal modification level of up to 20% for some peptides in S-phase, as shown with FLEXIQuant (Singh et al., 2009) which determines the absolute extent of modification.
evidence: This is an inference to explain the difference, with citation to Singh et al., 2009.

claim: The FLEXIQuant-LF approach provides the extent of modification relative to the given reference time point.
source: Thus, we emphasize that the FLEXIQuant-LF approach provides the extent of modification relative to the given reference time point.
evidence: This describes a key characteristic of FLEXIQuant-LF.

claim: FLEXIQuant-LF has an advantage over the conventional FLEXIQuant implementation in that the analysis can easily be performed on all proteins within a sample provided a minimum of five peptides was quantified.
source: FLEXIQuant-LF has an advantage over the conventional FLEXIQuant implementation in that the analysis can easily be performed on all proteins within a sample (provided a minimum of five peptides was quantified to allow for linear regression).
evidence: This describes an advantage of FLEXIQuant-LF over the original method.

claim: The analysis was extended to all other APC/C proteins of which sufficient peptides were reliably quantified: APC1, APC4, APC7, APC10, CDC16, CDC20, and CDC23.
source: Here, we extended our analysis to all other APC/C proteins of which sufficient peptides were reliably quantified in our data, namely APC1 (Figure 3) and APC4, APC7, APC10, CDC16, CDC20, and CDC23 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the extension of the analysis to additional APC/C proteins, as shown in Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: By applying FLEXIQuant-LF, between zero (APC4, APC10) and seven peptides (APC1) per protein were classified as likely differentially modified.
source: By applying FLEXIQuant-LF, we classified between zero (APC4, APC10) and seven peptides (APC1) per protein as likely differentially modified and between zero (APC4, APC10, CDC20) and four peptides (APC1) per protein as possibly differentially modified (summary in Table 1 and Table 2).
evidence: This summarizes the FLEXIQuant-LF classification results for all analyzed APC/C proteins.

claim: Between zero (APC4, APC10, CDC20) and four peptides (APC1) per protein were classified as possibly differentially modified.
source: By applying FLEXIQuant-LF, we classified between zero (APC4, APC10) and seven peptides (APC1) per protein as likely differentially modified and between zero (APC4, APC10, CDC20) and four peptides (APC1) per protein as possibly differentially modified (summary in Table 1 and Table 2).
evidence: This summarizes the FLEXIQuant-LF classification results for all analyzed APC/C proteins.

claim: 54 peptides corresponding to APC1 were quantified with 39% sequence coverage.
source: From APC1, we quantified 54 peptides (sequence coverage: 39%) in total, of which four peptides were classified as outlier based on their raw scores and were excluded from further analysis (930LVVWMTNVGFTLR942, 943DLETLPFGIALPIR956, 1546TGGEMNYGFHLAHHMALGLLFLGGGR1571 and 1618LLVPVDVDTNTPCamYALLEVTYK1639).
evidence: This describes the quantification results for APC1.

claim: Four APC1 peptides were classified as outliers and excluded from further analysis.
source: From APC1, we quantified 54 peptides (sequence coverage: 39%) in total, of which four peptides were classified as outlier based on their raw scores and were excluded from further analysis (930LVVWMTNVGFTLR942, 943DLETLPFGIALPIR956, 1546TGGEMNYGFHLAHHMALGLLFLGGGR1571 and 1618LLVPVDVDTNTPCamYALLEVTYK1639).
evidence: This describes the outlier removal in the APC1 analysis.

claim: Out of 50 remaining APC1 peptides, seven peptides were classified as likely differentially modified and four peptides as possibly differentially modified.
source: Out of the remaining 50 peptides, seven peptides were classified as likely differentially modified and four peptides as possibly differentially modified (Figure 3, magenta and blue bars, respectively).
evidence: This describes the FLEXIQuant-LF classification results for APC1, as shown in Figure 3.

claim: Phosphorylated peptides were identified in the DDA data for five of the seven likely and for three out of four possibly differentially modified APC1 peptides.
source: We identified phosphorylated peptides in the DDA data for five of the seven likely and for three out of four possibly differentially modified peptides (Figure 3, orange stars).
evidence: This describes the PTM identification results for APC1, as shown in Figure 3.

claim: The APC1 peptide 311GDSPVTSPFQNYSSIHQSR330 was classified as likely differentially modified by FLEXIQuant-LF, and multiple modifications have been reported in previous studies.
source: We also classified the peptide 311GDSPVTSPFQNYSSIHQSR330 as likely differentially modified by our FLEXIQuant-LF analysis, although no modified cognate peptides were identified in the DDA data. However, multiple modifications, that is phosphorylations on S313, T316, S317, Y322 and S324, have been reported in previous studies (Hornbeck et al., 2015) (indicated by a yellow star in Figure 3).
evidence: This describes validation of a FLEXIQuant-LF result using literature evidence, with citation to Hornbeck et al., 2015, as shown in Figure 3.

claim: For two consecutive APC1 peptides (1070LLQLCamQR1076 and 1077TMALPVGR1084), no published evidence of PTMs was found, but a hitherto undiscovered phosphorylation at threonine 1077 could explain the observed intensity reduction.
source: For one likely (1070LLQLCamQR1076) and one possibly differentially modified peptide (1077TMALPVGR1084), we could not find published evidence of PTMs within the sequence of those two peptides. Interestingly, these are consecutive peptides with the latter one starting with a threonine residue (AA 1077). A hitherto undiscovered phosphorylation at this threonine residue could lead to a highly increased missed cleavage which would be consistent with the observed intensity reduction of both peptides.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of FLEXIQuant-LF results for which no literature evidence was found.

claim: A more detailed analysis of APC1 identified two regions within the protein that appear to have different modification kinetics.
source: A more detailed analysis of the peptide-resolved modification dynamics observed in APC1 identified two regions within the protein that appear to have different modification kinetics (Figure 3).
evidence: This describes an observation from the FLEXIQuant-LF analysis, as shown in Figure 3.

claim: Peptides in the N-terminal part of APC1 ranging from residues 285–368 showed a degree of modification of 29–31% after 4 hr, 63–68% after 8 hr and between 70% and 71% after 10 hr.
source: Peptides in the N-terminal part ranging from residues 285–368 (four peptides), showed a degree of modification of 29–31% after 4 hr, 63–68% after 8 hr and between 70% and 71% after 10 hr.
evidence: This describes the quantification of modification extent for a specific region of APC1.

claim: Peptides in a more C-terminal domain of APC1 spanning residues 680–739 showed slower modification kinetics and a lower degree of modification at 10 hr.
source: In contrast, the peptides in a more C-terminal domain spanning residues 680–739 (three peptides) showed slower modification kinetics and a lower degree of modification at 10 hr. After 4 hr, 17–22% change in modification status was observed. The extent of modification changed between 39% and 57% after 8 hr, and 49–64% after 10 hr.
evidence: This describes the quantification of modification extent for another region of APC1.

claim: Tools to study the peptide-resolved modification dynamics in a quantitative manner will greatly improve the current understanding of biological processes.
source: These data demonstrate that tools to study the peptide-resolved modification dynamics in a quantitative manner will greatly improve the current understanding of biological processes.
evidence: This is an inference about the broader impact of tools like FLEXIQuant-LF.

claim: Over 1000 runs, FLEXIQuant-LF yielded ambiguous results for 6 out of 81 samples when using one RANSAC initiation.
source: Over 1000 runs FLEXIQuant-LF yielded ambiguous results for 6 out of 81 samples when using one RANSAC initiation.
evidence: This describes the reproducibility testing results.

claim: In all six ambiguous cases, two distinct outcomes were observed.
source: In all six cases, two distinct outcomes were observed.
evidence: This describes the nature of the ambiguous results.

claim: To improve reproducibility, the RANSAC algorithm was initiated multiple times within a single run and the best model based on r2 score was selected.
source: To improve the reproducibility, we initiated the RANSAC algorithm multiple times within a single run (1, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, and 100) and selected the best model (based on r2 score).
evidence: This describes a methodological improvement to enhance reproducibility.

claim: Using 30 RANSAC initiations and selecting the best model resulted in 44 suboptimal outcomes in 81,000 runs of FLEXIQuant-LF (0.05%).
source: Overall, using 30 RANSAC initiations and selecting the best model resulted in 44 suboptimal outcomes in 81,000 runs of FLEXIQuant-LF (0.05%).
evidence: This describes the improved reproducibility with multiple RANSAC initiations.

claim: The results confirm the benefits of multiple RANSAC initiations and demonstrate a very high reproducibility of the developed approach.
source: These results confirm the benefits of multiple RANSAC initiations and demonstrate a very high reproducibility of the developed approach.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the reproducibility testing data.

claim: Based on reproducibility testing findings, the default number of RANSAC initiations in FLEXIQuant-LF was set to 30.
source: Based on these finding, the default number of RANSAC initiations in FLEXIQuant-LF was set to 30 but can be changed by the user.
evidence: This describes a software design decision based on the reproducibility testing.

claim: The quality of FLEXIQuant-LF classification and quantification was tested on an independent DIA dataset from Bruderer et al., 2017.
source: We also tested the quality of FLEXIQuant-LF classification and quantification on an independent DIA dataset (Bruderer et al., 2017).
evidence: This describes the validation approach using an independent dataset, with citation to Bruderer et al., 2017.

claim: After stringent filtering, 122 proteins without detected modifications and with unique and unambiguous associations to peptides were selected for in silico modification.
source: After stringent filtering 122 proteins without detected modifications and with unique and unambiguous associations to peptides were selected for in silico modification, that is intensities of single peptides were reduced to simulate the presence of modified peptide species.
evidence: This describes the validation methodology using in silico modifications.

claim: For each protein, four peptides were randomly chosen and their intensity adjusted by a random change factor for each replicate resulting in 1574 total FLEXIQuant-LF runs.
source: For each protein, four peptides were randomly chosen, and their intensity adjusted by a random change factor for each replicate resulting in 1574 total FLEXIQuant-LF runs (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This describes the validation methodology.

claim: RM score changes showed a high correlation with the in-silico intensity change factors (Pearson's r = 0.98).
source: RM score changes showed a high correlation with the in-silico intensity change factors (Pearson's r = 0.98, Figure 4C).
evidence: This describes the validation results showing high accuracy, as shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The classes of likely not differentially modified and likely differentially modified peptides showed near optimal performance with sensitivity and precision values at 97.5% and 99.1%, and 100.0% and 96.1%, respectively.
source: The classes of likely not differentially modified and likely differentially modified peptides also showed near optimal performance with sensitivity and precision values at 97.5% and 99.1%, and 100.0% and 96.1%, respectively, while the class of possibly differentially modified peptides with hard-to-define borders showed reduced performance with a sensitivity of 77.2% and precision of 88.6% (Figure 4D).
evidence: This describes the classification performance metrics, as shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The class of possibly differentially modified peptides showed reduced performance with a sensitivity of 77.2% and precision of 88.6%.
source: The classes of likely not differentially modified and likely differentially modified peptides also showed near optimal performance with sensitivity and precision values at 97.5% and 99.1%, and 100.0% and 96.1%, respectively, while the class of possibly differentially modified peptides with hard-to-define borders showed reduced performance with a sensitivity of 77.2% and precision of 88.6% (Figure 4D).
evidence: This describes the classification performance metrics, as shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The decrease in accuracy for the possibly differentially modified class likely reflects more on the definition criteria of the middle group than on the performance of the method.
source: This decrease in accuracy likely reflects more on the definition criteria of the middle group than on the performance of the method.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the classification performance results.

claim: Overall quantification errors were low with a mean error of 0.020 (SD = 0.058, <0.1 for 94.7% of cases).
source: Overall, quantification errors were low with a mean error of 0.020 (SD = 0.058,<0.1 for 94.7% of cases, Figure 4E).
evidence: This describes the quantification accuracy, as shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Quantification errors in proteins with fewer peptides did not deviate from proteins with more peptides and were within a very small error margin of modification extent of <5%.
source: Quantification errors in proteins with fewer peptides (n = 5–7: μ = 0.027, SD = 0.072) did not deviate from proteins with more peptides (n = 8–10: μ = 0.010, SD = 0.020; n = 11–13: μ = 0.013, SD = 0.026; n = 14–17: μ = 0.006, SD = 0.012) and were within a very small error margin of modification extent of <5% (Figure 4F).
evidence: This describes the robustness of quantification across different numbers of peptides, as shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Outliers in quantification errors are rare (<5%) and can be attributed to the random selection and simulation effects of the assessment approach.
source: Outliers are rare (<5%) and can be attributed to the random selection and simulation effects of the assessment approach.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the outliers observed in the validation.

claim: For APC15 and APC16, the number of reliably quantified peptides were 1 and 3, respectively, below the threshold of five quantifiable peptides.
source: For the two smallest APC/C subunits, namely APC15 and APC16, the number of reliably quantified peptides were 1 and 3, respectively, that is below the described threshold of five quantifiable peptides, making the above described FLEXIQuant-LF analysis nonapplicable.
evidence: This describes a limitation encountered for small proteins.

claim: If proteins are known to have invariable expression/abundance profiles over the considered time period or between different conditions, the peptides of multiple proteins can be analyzed together by treating this set of proteins as one 'superprotein'.
source: However, if proteins are known to have invariable expression/abundance profiles over the considered time period or between different conditions of interest, as for example observed for the core components of the APC/C, we hypothesized that the peptides of multiple proteins can be analyzed together by treating this set of proteins with invariable abundance as one 'superprotein'.
evidence: This describes the rationale for the 'superprotein' approach.

claim: The 'superprotein' approach would expand the FLEXIQuant-LF approach to smaller proteins and allow for the identification and quantification of differential modification of proteins with less than five quantified peptides.
source: This would expand the FLEXIQuant-LF approach to smaller proteins and allow for the identification and quantification of differential modification of proteins with less than five quantified peptides that could not be analyzed by the normal FLEXIQuant-LF implementation otherwise.
evidence: This describes the benefit of the 'superprotein' approach.

claim: To test the 'superprotein' approach, all reliably quantified APC/C proteins except CDC20 were analyzed in a combined fashion as a 'superprotein'.
source: To test this 'superprotein' approach, we applied FLEXIQuant-LF to analyze all reliably quantified APC/C proteins in our data in a combined fashion as a 'superprotein', namely APC1, APC4, APC5, APC7, APC10, APC15, APC16, CDC16, CDC23, and CDC27. CDC20 was excluded from this 'superprotein' approach as it is known that this APC/C regulator displays changing affinity to the APC/C during the M-phase of the cell cycle, that is its abundance within the APC/C changes during the investigated time period (Fang et al., 1999).
evidence: This describes the 'superprotein' approach testing, with citation to Fang et al., 1999.

claim: The 'superprotein' strategy was validated by comparing its results to the results of the FLEXIQuant-LF analysis of the individual proteins for all proteins that could be analyzed with both strategies.
source: We validated the 'superprotein' strategy by comparing its results to the results of the FLEXIQuant-LF analysis of the individual proteins for all proteins that could be analyzed with both strategies.
evidence: This describes the validation approach for the 'superprotein' strategy.

claim: The two approaches (individual protein and 'superprotein') resulted in identical classification of peptides as well as near identical quantification of the modification extent (mean RM score difference = 2.45E-10, r2 = 1).
source: The two approaches resulted in identical classification of peptides as well as near identical quantification of the modification extent (mean RM score difference = 2.45E-10, r2 = 1), demonstrating the applicability of the 'superprotein' strategy (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This describes the validation results for the 'superprotein' strategy.

claim: The FLEXIQuant-LF analysis of APC15 and APC16 using the 'superprotein' approach revealed that all four peptides associated with these two small proteins are likely not differentially modified.
source: The FLEXIQuant-LF analysis of APC15 and APC16 using the 'superprotein' approach revealed that all four peptides associated with these two small proteins not amenable to the conventional FLEXIQuant-LF approach are likely not differentially modified (Supplementary file 2 and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This describes the results of applying the 'superprotein' approach to APC15 and APC16, as shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The results for APC15 and APC16 are in accordance with the literature where no cell cycle-dependent differential modifications have been described for the detected protein domains.
source: These results are in accordance with the literature where, to the best of our knowledge, no cell cycle-dependent differential modifications in APC15 and APC16 have been described for the detected protein domains (Hornbeck et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes concordance with literature, with citation to Hornbeck et al., 2015.

claim: FLEXIQuant-LF is based on robust linear regression, as implemented in the RANSAC algorithm.
source: Our FLEXIQuant-LF is based on robust linear regression, as implemented in the RANSAC algorithm.
evidence: This describes the algorithmic foundation of FLEXIQuant-LF.

claim: Linear regression requires a certain number of data points to yield meaningful results and becomes more accurate with increasing number of data points.
source: In general, linear regression requires a certain number of data points to yield meaningful results and becomes more accurate with increasing number of data points.
evidence: This is a general principle of linear regression.

claim: FLEXIQuant-LF becomes more powerful with increasing numbers of unique peptides that can be identified for the proteins of interest.
source: Thus, FLEXIQuant-LF becomes more powerful with increasing numbers of unique peptides that can be identified for the proteins of interest.
evidence: This is a logical consequence of the linear regression principle applied to FLEXIQuant-LF.

claim: The minimum number of unique peptides required for a FLEXIQuant-LF analysis was set to five.
source: We set the minimum number of unique peptides required for a FLEXIQuant-LF analysis to five, although a larger number of peptides will provide more robust results.
evidence: This describes a design decision for the FLEXIQuant-LF tool.

claim: A larger number of peptides will provide more robust FLEXIQuant-LF results.
source: We set the minimum number of unique peptides required for a FLEXIQuant-LF analysis to five, although a larger number of peptides will provide more robust results.
evidence: This is a logical consequence of the linear regression principle.

claim: The 'superprotein' approach addresses the limitation of requiring a minimum number of peptides.
source: Addressing this limitation, we introduce the 'superprotein' approach.
evidence: This describes the purpose of the 'superprotein' approach.

claim: FLEXIQuant-LF was applied to a time series experiment in the presented proof-of-concept study.
source: In the presented proof-of-concept study, we applied FLEXIQuant-LF to a time series experiment.
evidence: This describes the type of experiment used for proof-of-concept.

claim: FLEXIQuant-LF can also be applied to study protein modification differences between different experimental conditions or cohorts in general.
source: However, FLEXIQuant-LF can also be applied to study protein modification differences between different experimental conditions or cohorts in general, e.g. comparing diseased vs. healthy individuals or testing the effect of different drugs.
evidence: This describes the broader applicability of FLEXIQuant-LF beyond time series experiments.

claim: FLEXIQuant-LF only determines the extent of differential modification of a peptide relative to the reference based on the unmodified counterparts.
source: As FLEXIQuant-LF only determines the extent of differential modification of a peptide relative to the reference based on the unmodified counterparts, quantification of the absolute abundance of the modification still requires an isotopically labeled internal standard.
evidence: This describes a limitation of FLEXIQuant-LF compared to absolute quantification methods.

claim: Quantification of the absolute abundance of the modification still requires an isotopically labeled internal standard.
